q: The frequency of radiation is $1.0 \cdot 10^{15}\,\text{Hz}$. What is the energy of one photon?

A sodium plate ($W = 2.28\,\text{eV}$) is illuminated with yellow light, $\lambda = 590\,\text{nm}$, and no electrons are released. Which helps: making the yellow light brighter or changing to blue light, $\lambda = 470\,\text{nm}$? Why?
a: Blue light. One electron receives the energy of one photon, and the photon energy of yellow light, $2.10\,\text{eV}$, is smaller than the work function, so making it brighter only brings more photons that are too weak. The photon energy of blue light, $2.64\,\text{eV}$, is greater than $2.28\,\text{eV}$, so electrons are released. The frequency decides whether electrons are released; making light of the same colour brighter only increases their number once they are released.
